purpose: Bounded U.S. Department of Labor wage-recovery route showing that agency recovery still requires worker location, notice, identity verification, claim effort, payment access, and later use.

events.geography: United States; U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division
events.date_precision: current official Workers Owed Wages route observed in the public agency page; operational rules and payment process can change
events.denominator: Workers for whom WHD has recovered unpaid wages; no single public episode denominator or same-worker outcome panel
events.method: Structured extraction from the official WHD Workers Owed Wages public route and claim instructions
events.missingness: Individual worker identity, amount, address history, notice receipt, claim effort, identity documents, payment date, cashing, fees, adequacy, household effect, later work, trust, recurrence, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: A labor-law violation produces unpaid wages that WHD may recover and hold for the worker while attempting to locate and notify them
events.alternatives_before_action: The public route does not observe whether a worker used an employer complaint, private claim, union, legal aid, other job, savings, or non-use alternative before the agency route
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Agency recovery creates a possible monetary remedy, but access requires searching the WOW system, verifying identity, supplying contact information, signing a claim form, uploading documents, and using a payment channel
events.choice_or_response: WHD attempts location and notice; the worker must search, verify identity, submit contact information and a signed claim with documents; WHD processes the claim and sends payment
events.person_or_actor_with_control: WHD controls recovery, notice attempts, holding period, claim processing, and payment; the worker controls search, contact, identity submission, and claim completion; Treasury receives unclaimed funds after the stated holding period
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: WHD operates the Workers Owed Wages application, attempts to locate and notify workers, holds wages for three years when a worker cannot be found, and sends remaining funds to the Treasury after that period
events.remedy_receipt: The public route describes claim processing and electronic payment but does not establish that any particular worker found, claimed, received, cashed, or adequately used the money
events.durability_followup: No same-worker public follow-up records later household security, debt or food relief, continued work, recurrence, trust, switching, or exit
events.immediate_outcome: A formal wage-recovery and recipient-reachability route is operationally specified
events.protected_outcome: The route preserves a path from institutional recovery to worker claim and payment, and it provides a searchable channel for workers who know or suspect money is waiting
events.sacrificed_outcome: Workers may bear search, notice, identity, documentation, time, and payment-access burdens; workers who remain unreachable can lose direct access even though the institution records the funds as recovered
events.cost_risk_transfer: The public recovery route shifts final connection and claim work partly to the worker while preserving institutional custody and eventual Treasury disposition
events.later_outcome: The route ends publicly at claim processing and payment instructions, not at verified receipt, adequacy, household recovery, trust, or exit
events.meaning_and_attribution: The institution frames the route as recovery of legally owed wages; worker interpretation, legitimacy, dignity, and trust are not measured
events.public_or_collective_response: A public search-and-claim route is visible; no worker-level collective or political response is measured
events.counterexample: Recovered wages can be institutionally held and searchable while remaining practically unusable to a worker who cannot be located, notified, verified, or reached through the payment process
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division Workers Owed Wages page, checked 2026-09-19; route rules are public institutional descriptions, not worker-level outcome data

events.geography: United States; U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division Workers Owed Wages route
events.date_precision: Official route states electronic payments began October 1, 2025; current instructions checked 2026-09-19
events.denominator: Workers receiving or expecting back wages through the WOW route; no public recipient-level transition denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from current official WHD Workers Owed Wages payment instructions
events.missingness: No recipient identity, paper-check failure, update effort, claim submission, payment date, delivery, cashing, fee, adequacy, household effect, or later work outcome is retained
events.exposure: Workers previously receiving back wages by paper check are instructed to update their information because payments are made electronically
events.alternatives_before_action: A worker may update payment information, seek agency help, use other income or credit, or fail to continue the route; those alternatives and their feasibility are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Electronic payment may speed or standardize delivery, but it creates an account/contact-update and digital identity requirement for people whose prior paper-check route may no longer continue
events.choice_or_response: The worker must confirm details, search the employer and name, provide contact information, upload a signed claim form, create a login.gov account, and submit identity documentation; the public record does not show completion
events.person_or_actor_with_control: WHD controls the payment channel and claim process; workers control information updates and document submission within their access, identity, time, and technology constraints
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: WHD moved the route toward electronic payment and specifies identity/document upload and approximately six-week processing instructions
events.remedy_receipt: The channel and processing expectation are public, but no recipient-level electronic delivery, cashing, correction, or adequacy is observed
events.durability_followup: No same-worker follow-up shows whether the payment route remained usable or changed later security, work, trust, switching, or exit
events.immediate_outcome: Wage recovery now includes a documented payment-channel transition that can shift final access work toward digital identity, current contact information, and account readiness
events.protected_outcome: Electronic payment may protect delivery continuity for workers who can update and verify their information
events.sacrificed_outcome: Workers without stable contact, identity documents, digital access, or account readiness may face delay or nonreceipt, but the affected population is not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The transition may reduce paper-payment handling while transferring update, documentation, login, and digital-access risk to recipients
events.later_outcome: Successful payment, cashing, adequacy, household relief, continued work, trust, switching, and exit remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No worker-level interpretation of electronic payment, privacy, dignity, fairness, or institutional legitimacy is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: The agency publishes the transition and claim route; worker complaints, organizing, and political response are not linked
events.counterexample: Electronic payment can be easier for one worker and a barrier for another; the route description does not identify which experience occurred
events.source_and_uncertainty: Current official WHD Workers Owed Wages instructions; operational guidance is not recipient-level outcome data

arrows.to: WHD recovery and custody of wages
arrows.evidence: WHD states that when it finds violations it recovers unpaid wages on behalf of employees
arrows.counterexample: Agency recovery does not establish that a named worker received the money
arrows.remaining_gap: Case identifier, worker amount, recovery date, and worker-level attribution

arrows.evidence: WHD says it makes efforts to locate and notify workers and provides a searchable Workers Owed Wages application
arrows.counterexample: A route can exist without showing whether the worker was found, notified, or able to respond
arrows.remaining_gap: Notice delivery, comprehension, address continuity, search effort, and administrative burden

arrows.to: claim submission and electronic payment processing
arrows.evidence: The official instructions require employer search, name verification, contact information, a signed claim form, identity documents, and processing before payment
arrows.counterexample: Instructions describe an available route, not successful completion or payment
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker completion, time cost, document access, eligibility dispute, payment date, fees, and cashing

arrows.from: worker remains unreachable after the holding period
arrows.evidence: WHD states that it holds wages for three years while trying to locate the employee and then must send the money to the U.S. Treasury if the person remains unlocated
arrows.counterexample: Treasury disposition is not worker receipt or proof that the worker chose not to claim
arrows.remaining_gap: Reason for non-location, later claimability, worker notice, and practical loss

arrows.from: claim processing or reported wage recovery
arrows.to: worker receipt, adequacy, household security, trust, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public route provides processing and payment instructions but no same-worker follow-up on receipt, use, or later life outcomes
arrows.counterexample: A payment instruction or agency recovery statistic can coexist with non-receipt, delay, insufficient amount, or unresolved household loss
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-worker receipt, amount, timing, cashing, remaining loss, household outcome, later work, trust, switching, and exit

arrows.evidence: WHD instructs people receiving back wages by paper check to update their information because payments are made electronically beginning October 1, 2025
arrows.counterexample: An update instruction does not show that paper checks failed or that every recipient needed the same intervention
arrows.remaining_gap: Recipient-level transition status, update effort, contact continuity, and payment consequence

arrows.to: claim processing and electronic payment route
arrows.evidence: The current instructions require contact information, a signed claim form, login.gov access, and identity documentation before WHD processing and payment
arrows.counterexample: A specified process does not establish successful submission, acceptance, or a six-week completion for a named worker
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker completion, document access, processing decision, payment date, and administrative burden

arrows.evidence: WHD states that after the claim form is submitted it will process the claim in approximately six weeks and send owed wages, but publishes no recipient delivery or later-life follow-up
arrows.counterexample: Electronic payment can be sent without being accessible, cashed, adequate, or sufficient to change household security
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-worker delivery, cashing, amount, fees, remaining loss, household security, continued work, trust, and exit

boundary: This ledger closes an institutional wage-recovery and reachability architecture, not a worker-level payment or recovery outcome. It must not be pooled with case-level reported receipts or interpreted as a recovery rate.
storage_boundary: No worker, wage, claim, identity, bank, or restricted data is retained; only the public institutional route and its explicit unresolved recipient/outcome stages are represented.
